events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.26 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip contained one off-route segment: 14:27–14:37, 6.47 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 this segment counts as a deviation and must be tested against RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5; no threshold applies [RD-1].

RD-5 does not exempt it. The segment started at 14:27 [F3], while the driver asked about "going round via West Coast Highway" only at 14:29 [F7] and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 14:30 [F8]. The consent therefore does not pre-date the start of the segment, and a change communicated after the driver has already left the optimal route is not consent under RD-5 [RD-5].

RD-4 does not exempt it either. There is no traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch at all [F12]; the only records are speed bands 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE [F10] and 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road [F11], both above the band 1–2 congestion range, and a band record alone cannot exempt a segment [RD-4]. The driver's congestion explanation is accordingly withdrawn and unsupported.

No rider-named stop applies: the rider named no place and no stop preceded the segment, so RD-3 gives no exemption [RD-3]. Weather is fair, 0.0 mm rain [F13], and there is no surge (1.0×) [F5], so nothing enlarges or excuses the deviation.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the deviation enters the fare through distance [F6]. The per-km rate is distance fare ÷ distance km: $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.4099/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. The refund is the extra km of the unexempt segment only: 5.15 km × $1.4099/km = $7.26 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual difference between the $8.35 excess-distance component billed [F4] and the segment sum is map-matching residue and is not refunded [RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F15], so no account flag is added [RD-6].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your route dispute and found part of the trip took a detour worth refunding. The trip included a stretch of about 6.5 km where the usual route is about 1.3 km, and the extra distance added to your metered fare. A question about going a different way was asked after that stretch had already begun, so it doesn't count as agreeing to it in advance. We're issuing you a $7.26 Ryde voucher for the extra distance. It's applied to your account as a voucher, not cash or card. Thanks for flagging this.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on one of your metered trips and found a stretch that counted as a detour from the best route. The offer to go a different way came after you had already left the best route, and no traffic or road records support the alternative route, so that stretch doesn't qualify as agreed or exempt. A $7.26 Ryde voucher is being issued to the rider for the extra distance. This is recorded on your file as a route breach. No account flag is added at this stage.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.26 Ryde voucher (NS-7) to the rider for the unexempt off-route segment on this metered RydeTAXI trip; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip contained one off-route segment: 14:27–14:37, 6.47 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 this segment counts as a deviation and must be tested against RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5; no threshold applies [RD-1].

RD-5 does not exempt it. The segment started at 14:27 [F3], while the driver asked about "going round via West Coast Highway" only at 14:29 [F7] and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 14:30 [F8]. The consent therefore does not pre-date the start of the segment, and a change communicated after the driver has already left the optimal route is not consent under RD-5 [RD-5].

RD-4 does not exempt it either. There is no traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch at all [F12]; the only records are speed bands 4 (30–39 km/h) on the AYE [F10] and 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road [F11], both above the band 1–2 congestion range, and a band record alone cannot exempt a segment [RD-4]. The driver's congestion explanation is accordingly withdrawn and unsupported.

No rider-named stop applies: the rider named no place and no stop preceded the segment, so RD-3 gives no exemption [RD-3]. Weather is fair, 0.0 mm rain [F13], and there is no surge (1.0×) [F5], so nothing enlarges or excuses the deviation.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the deviation enters the fare through distance [F6]. The per-km rate is distance fare ÷ distance km: $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.4099/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. The refund is the extra km of the unexempt segment only: 5.15 km × $1.4099/km = $7.26 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The residual difference between the $8.35 excess-distance component billed [F4] and the segment sum is map-matching residue and is not refunded [RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F15], so no account flag is added [RD-6].

The agreed mention of West Coast Highway [F7] cannot exempt a segment begun before the request [F3][F8]; the 5.15 km extra remains billable under RD-2 rather than no_action [RD-5][RD-2].
Correct but immaterial to the outcome: the driver's 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F15] means RD-6 adds no flag_account action [RD-6].

Segment therefore unexempt and refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (−$7.26).
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows a single off-route segment from 14:27 to 14:37 in which 6.47 km was driven where the optimal route covers only 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route.

The driver's consent message was sent at 14:29 (chat #1), i.e. after the off-route segment had already begun at 14:27, so the rider's 14:30 'Sure, go ahead' reply was not agreement given before the deviation and does not exempt the segment.

The driver's claimed justification is traffic on the Ayer Rajah Expressway, but the only traffic records are speed bands 4 (30-39 km/h) and 5 (40-49 km/h), with no incident on the optimal route; there is no traffic incident fact to support a justified reroute.

Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra distance was billed: the total charged is $31.56 with distance $20.43 for 14.5 km at $1.41/km, and excess distance billed $8.35 (5.9 km x $1.41/km); a refund of the unexempt 5.15 km at $1.41/km equals $7.26.
No surcharge applies to inflate the refund and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather-related excuse exists for the deviation.
The driver's 90-day history shows 2 disputes and 0 upheld with no route disputes upheld, so the 90-day threshold for an account flag is not met and no flag_account is requested.

weaknesses: The rider did reply 'Sure, go ahead' at 14:30 (F8) and the driver's statement (F9) claims the change was communicated; the other side will argue this was consent to the West Coast Highway route, and RD-5 only defeats that because the timestamp 14:30 is after the segment start 14:27 (F3).

The trip estimate was 8.6 km / 14 min but the metered total of 14.5 km / 22.2 min (F1, F2) could be explained by congestion rather than deviation; however, the only traffic facts are speed bands 4-5 on AYE and Jurong Town Hall Road with no incident (F10, F11, F12), which does not establish 'reasonable cause' under RD-4.
The rider's own profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld (F14), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of disputing fares.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment on the GPS track (F3, 14:27–14:37, +5.15 km) began after the rider's explicit consent message, so the route change is covered by RD-5 rather than being an unexplained deviation.

The driver asked before committing to the alternative route and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead" at 14:30, so there was an agreement reached before the change took effect as required by Ryde's procedure for route changes.

The off-route stretch is the West Coast Highway detour the rider approved; as a mutually agreed routing it does not count as an unexempted off-route segment and the segment attracts no_action under RD-5.

RYDE-taxi metered billing follows actual distance (F6: distance $20.43 for 14.5 km at $1.41/km; F4: excess distance component $8.35), so the disputed amount at stake is $8.35, not the whole $31.56 fare.

The driver's reason for the detour was congestion, and while the Ayer Rajah Expressway band 4 record (F10) and the absence of any recorded incident (F12) mean RD-4 exemption is not made out, that fact alone does not defeat RD-5, which is the clause the rider's consent satisfies.
The driver has 344 trips in the last 90 days, 2 disputes and 0 upheld (route: 0), so there is no repeated-violation history that would support a flag_account action against him.

weaknesses: The consent came at 14:30, three minutes after the off-route segment started at 14:27 (F3 vs F8), so the rider will argue the driver turned off first and told him after — exactly the sequence RD-5 says does not count as consent (the rider's own complaint says this).
The rider will also argue the agreed scope was only "West Coast Highway" and not the full 5.15 km / 1194 m swing off the optimal route recorded in F3, so the detour exceeded what he agreed to.

There is no RD-4 traffic exemption: F12 records no incidents at all and F10 shows band 4 (30–39 km/h), above the band 1–2 congestion definition, so if RD-5 consent is rejected the whole 5.15 km segment becomes billable and the RD-2 refund would be computed on it (F4 shows $8.35 of excess distance).
F1 shows the detour is large in scale (+69% distance) and F2 shows +8.4 min, which supports the rider's narrative that the driver wandered rather than taking a minor alternative.

points.response: The GPS off-route segment starts at 14:27 (F3) while the rider's consent 'Sure, go ahead' is timestamped 14:30 (F8) and the driver's own request 14:29 (F7); RD-5 requires consent before the segment starts, so this segment is not exempted.

There was no agreement before the change took effect: the driver's message (F7, 14:29) and the rider's reply (F8, 14:30) both postdate the segment start at 14:27 (F3), and RD-5 expressly treats a post-deviation notice as not consent.

RD-5 only exempts the stretch the rider agreed to while still on the optimal route, and here the rider's consent scope cannot cover a segment begun two minutes earlier that swung up to 1194 m off-route (F3, F7, F8); the remaining unexempted 5.15 km stays billable under RD-2.

Conceded: the metered RydeTAXI billing means the disputable sum is the excess-distance component, and we agree the ceiling is $8.35 (F4, F6); our RD-2 computation on the 5.15 km unexempted segment is $7.26, which is within that cap.

RD-5 and RD-4 are separate escape routes and RD-4 is not made out: F12 records no incident and F10 shows AYE at band 4 (30-39 km/h), above the band 1-2 congestion definition; without RD-5 consent the segment is unexempted under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2.
We do not contest this and do not request flag_account; F15 shows the driver has 2 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld with 0 route disputes, so the RD-6 repeated-violation threshold is not met.

The segment is real (F3) but its existence is not itself the finding; RD-1 requires the segment to be unexempt, and this one is claimed under RD-5 consent, so C1 only sets up the question C2 must answer.

The consent timeline cuts both ways: the off-route segment started 14:27 (F3) and the driver's request came 14:29 (F7) with the rider's 'Sure, go ahead' at 14:30 (F8), so on the clock consent is after the segment start; I do not contest that C2 defeats RD-5 for the initial turn-off, and my case therefore cannot rest on RD-5 for the whole segment.

Conceded on the traffic point: F12 records no incident at all and F10/F11 are bands 4–5, above the band 1–2 congestion definition, so no segment is exempted under RD-4 and I withdraw any reliance on the driver's congestion explanation.

The refund base is right but the amount is not contested at $7.26: the off-route segment added 5.15 km (F3) and the metered rate is $1.41/km (F4, F6: distance $20.43 for 14.5 km), so 5.15 x $1.41 = $7.26, which is the correct RD-2 figure on this metered RydeTAXI trip; only the unexempt segment's extra_km is refundable and the residual map-matching difference between the $8.35 excess billed (F4) and the segment sum is not.
Accepted: F5 shows surge 1.0x and F13 shows fair weather, 0.0 mm rain, so no surcharge or weather factor enlarges or excuses the deviation and the refund stays at the metered distance figure.

Agreed: F15 shows 344 trips in 90 days with 2 disputes and 0 upheld (route: 0), so RD-6 is not triggered and no flag_account should be added against the driver, keeping the outcome to the distance refund alone.
